system: IBM Quantum Nighthawk + Quantum-Centric Supercomputing Blueprint
key_facts: Nighthawk: 120-qubit processor, 20%+ greater connectivity than Heron via 218 tunable couplers
Handles up to 5,000 two-qubit gates now; target 7,500 gates by end of 2026, 10,000 in 2027
Quantum-Centric Supercomputing reference architecture published 2026-03-12: first blueprint for QPU+GPU+CPU integration
RIKEN+IBM demo: largest quantum simulation of iron-sulfur clusters via closed-loop Heron+Fugaku (152,064 nodes)
303-atom protein simulation demonstrated with the new architecture
Quantum advantage tracker launched (community-led, open): monitors advantage across observable estimation, variational problems, and classically-verifiable problems
mera_relevance: The quantum-centric supercomputing blueprint is directly relevant to how we might eventually run production MERA experiments: QPU handles the quantum circuit, classical HPC handles the Hamiltonian mat-vec (our current bottleneck). The blueprint formalizes the hybrid loop we already use. Nighthawk's 5,000-gate budget is below what we need for 5-layer 24q MERA with error mitigation, but the 7,500/10,000 gate targets in 2026-2027 are entering our range. Primary hardware target remains Helios due to fidelity advantages.
